judge_notes.opus: K won because it interprets rather than lists: 'at introductory prices matching its cheaper Argon model rather than a premium tier,' 'Alibaba answered within a day,' and 'The week's clearest caution came from NEAR AI' give hierarchy and a reason to care; its only blemish is an ambiguous 'it.' O lost on spec density and run-ons ('its 280B-total, 14B-active ERNIE 5.5 Flash Preview', 'its 33.1-billion-parameter MiniMax-H3-Image native 4K generator'), with L close behind for the same reason.
judge_notes.glm: Q won because it is the only summary with a narrative and a payoff: 'Alibaba answered within a day' gives the day a throughline, and it closes on a concrete security story ('a remote code execution flaw in the SGLang inference engine') that tells the reader why the day mattered beyond product news. P and J and L followed with clean structure and concrete detail, each docked only for list-burden in the opener. I lost worst because nearly every sentence is a 50-word spec stack ('280B-total, 14B-active') with no hierarchy, and R lost nearly as badly for spending its closer on disclaimers about evidence and test conditions rather than the news itself.
judge_notes.astra: M wins because its progression from model access to "packaging AI into customer-facing and productivity workflows" supplies an intelligible business takeaway in readable sentences; its vague availability and licensing distinctions keep it below exceptional. F is the closest challenger, with a concrete confidentiality failure explaining stakes, but its financing detour weakens cohesion. P loses because its opening expands through "while Anthropic launched its IPO roadshow" into a roughly 75-word accumulation of prices, benchmarks and financial mechanics; subsequent paragraphs never establish a controlling idea.
